MotivationMotivation
• Soot
– Pollutant, carcinogen, contributes to glacial melting
• Smoke point (SP) measures sooting propensity.
– Luminous flame length before smoke emission.
– Correlates w/ soot volume fraction and radiative loss fraction.
• Prediction: Non-buoyant flames don’t have smoke points.
– Residence time would not scale with flow rate.
•S m o k e points found aboard parabolic aircraft and space shuttle.pp p
• It is believed that residence time influences smoking behavior.

text:
ConclusionsConclusions
Over the presently tested range of fuel, ua, and d:
• Smoke point increases with increasing coflow velocitySmoke point increases with increasing coflow velocity.
• Smoke point decreases with increasing burner diameter.
• Fuel sooting propensities agree wi th those of buoyant flames.
– Propane < Ethylene < 50% Propylene < 75% Propylene < Propylene
• Ethylene less sooty than propane for 0.76 mm burner. (appears
as a different TSI for propane)
• LSP scales with fuel mass flow rate.
– Consistent with simplified theory.
23
– Second order effect: Longer LSP for low ua / uf .
– Coflow theory neglects radial velocity, v.
